title: Annotatio VI §.VII press: if Indignorum doctrine is slight, why Paul’s solicitude?
pass_a_gloss: But the Author presses, about to sustain the Necessity of the doctrine of the unworthy’s eating of Christ’s body: But if, he says, little or nothing is placed in the doctrine of the Eating of the unworthy, why did Paul explain it with such solicitude and care? Is it credible that the Apostle would have pursued a matter of slight moment with such zeal?
pass_b_english: He presses necessity: if the Indignorum doctrine matters little, why did Paul treat it with such care?
Would the Apostle chase a slight matter with that zeal?
source_text: At instat Autor, Necessitatem doctrinæ de indignorum manducatione corporis Christi sustentaturus: Quodsi, ait, in doctrina de Manducatione indignorum parum aut nihil situm est, cur eam Paulus tantâ sollicitudine curáque explicuit? Numne credibile, Apostolum exigui momenti rem, tantô studio persecuturum fuisse?
